prompt: A lab can run only two GPU jobs overnight. One job gives a reliable baseline, the other tests a risky reasoning intervention. Decide which measurements to collect so tomorrow's result is publishable even if the intervention fails.
rubric_items: preserve a reliable baseline measurement
compare the risky intervention against the baseline
record enough metrics to explain failure modes
state what remains publishable if the intervention fails
avoid spending both jobs on risky variants

prompt: A data pipeline fails once every few thousand records, but logs are too noisy and there are only two hours before a customer demo. Give a short triage plan that finds the likely cause without risking the demo.
rubric_items: isolate a minimal failing record or batch
reduce log noise with targeted instrumentation
protect the demo path with rollback or cached data
prioritize likely malformed input or schema drift
define a stop condition before the demo

prompt: A new model improves offline accuracy but triples latency in production. The team can either ship, rollback, or gate the release. Decide what to measure and what decision rule to use.
rubric_items: compare accuracy lift against latency cost
measure production tail latency not only average latency
include a gated or canary rollout option
define rollback thresholds
name user impact or reliability risk

prompt: A research result looks impressive, but the baseline used more tokens and a different prompt format. Design a quick falsification plan before anyone writes a public claim.
rubric_items: equalize token budget and prompt format
rerun the baseline and intervention on locked tasks
separate oracle best-of results from selected results
record regressions as well as wins
state what claim survives if the effect disappears

prompt: A training run is halfway complete when disk usage spikes and checkpoint writes start failing. Give a recovery plan that preserves reproducibility and avoids corrupting the best checkpoint.
rubric_items: stop or throttle writes before corrupting checkpoints
identify removable cache or temporary files
verify the latest good checkpoint before deleting anything
preserve config seeds and logs for reproducibility
resume from a validated checkpoint only

prompt: A customer dashboard shows wrong totals after a timezone migration. The team needs a fix today and a deeper root-cause analysis later. Plan the first response.
rubric_items: compare old and new timezone aggregation on sample accounts
patch or rollback the display path quickly
communicate scope and uncertainty to stakeholders
add tests around boundary times
separate immediate mitigation from root-cause follow-up

prompt: A model training run diverges after an optimizer change, but only one GPU is free for debugging. Decide the cheapest experiment sequence to isolate the cause.
rubric_items: reproduce with the smallest run that still diverges
compare old and new optimizer with fixed seed
check learning rate and gradient norms
change one variable at a time
stop once the cause is isolated

prompt: A benchmark score improves, but the qualitative outputs look generic and evasive. Decide how to test whether the system actually reasons better rather than gaming the scorer.
rubric_items: inspect examples where the score improved
add a rubric for specificity and causal diagnosis
measure regressions and evasive answers
use held-out tasks or adversarial prompts
separate verbosity from correctness

prompt: A warehouse has 17 shelves with 24 boxes each. Workers remove 3 carts with 18 boxes each. How many boxes remain? Answer with one integer.
A train travels 180 miles at 45 miles per hour, then stops for 30 minutes. How many total minutes pass? Answer with one integer.
A team has $240. Each sensor costs $35 and shipping is a fixed $25. What is the maximum number of sensors they can buy? Answer with one integer.
Start with 5. Double it, add 14, then multiply by 3. What is the result? Answer with one integer.
Three classes have 28, 31, and 26 students. If 12 students are absent total, how many students are present? Answer with one integer.
Five identical machines make 1200 parts in 8 hours. At the same rate, how many parts do 3 machines make in 6 hours? Answer with one integer.
A 7 by 9 grid has 13 cells blocked. How many cells are unblocked? Answer with one integer.
A notebook starts with 96 pages. Four sections use 17, 23, 8, and 19 pages. How many blank pages remain? Answer with one integer.
If D is before A, A is before B, and B is before C, what is the full order from first to last? Answer with the four letters separated by spaces.
A lamp starts off. It is toggled 5 times. Is it on or off at the end? Answer only on or off.
Start with the list red, blue, green. Swap the first and third items, then swap the second and third items. What is the final list?
All zargs are blicks. No blicks are morts. Can a zarg be a mort? Answer yes or no.
A code maps A to 1, B to 2, C to 3, and so on. What number does F map to? Answer with one integer.
Let f(x)=2x+3 and g(x)=x-5. What is f(g(10))? Answer with one integer.
A plant experiment changes only the amount of fertilizer and measures plant height. What is the independent variable? A) plant height B) amount of fertilizer C) pot color D) final leaf count
A fixed-volume gas is heated while the amount of gas stays the same. What generally happens to pressure? A) decreases B) stays exactly zero C) increases D) becomes unrelated to temperature
In standard DNA base pairing, adenine pairs with which base? A) cytosine B) thymine C) guanine D) uracil

A store sells notebooks in packs of 6. Mara buys 4 packs, gives 7 notebooks away, then splits the rest equally among 5 bins. How many notebooks are left over after making equal bins? Answer with one integer.

A 90-minute workshop has three talks of 14 minutes each and two breaks of 9 minutes each. The remaining time is split evenly into 3 Q&A sessions. How many minutes is each Q&A session? Answer with one integer.
A tank is 3/5 full. After adding 18 liters, it is 4/5 full. What is the full capacity of the tank in liters? Answer with one integer.

Nia is packing 48 apples. A note on the table says there are 9 oranges, but the oranges are not being packed. She sets aside 3 damaged apples, then puts the remaining apples into bags with 5 apples per bag. How many full apple bags can she make? Answer with one integer.

A club sold 17 adult tickets for 12 dollars each and 8 child tickets for 7 dollars each. A sponsor also donated 25 dollars, but that donation is not ticket revenue. How many dollars came from ticket sales? Answer with one integer.

Ravi read 18 pages on Monday. On Tuesday he read twice as many pages as Monday. On Wednesday he read 7 fewer pages than Tuesday. The book has 200 pages, but only count the pages read across those three days. How many pages did Ravi read? Answer with one integer.

There are 6 trays with 14 cookies on each tray. A label mentions 9 chocolate-chip cookies, but the question asks about all cookies. After 20 cookies are eaten, the remaining cookies are shared equally by 8 students. How many cookies does each student get? Answer with one integer.
A code starts at 9. If the current number is odd, triple it and add 1; if it is even, halve it. Apply this rule twice. What number results? Answer with one integer.
A display starts with the code K L M. Rotate the code one step left, then swap the final two letters. What code should be displayed? Answer with the three letters separated by spaces.
A display starts with the code P Q R S. Rotate the code one step right, then swap the first two letters. What code should be displayed? Answer with the four letters separated by spaces.
Start with the list cyan, magenta, yellow, black. Swap the first and fourth items, then swap the second and third items. What is the final list? Answer with the color words separated by spaces.

A retrieval-augmented answer cites three documents, but one citation contradicts the other two. The team has one hour before a customer review. Plan how to decide whether to ship, patch, or hold the answer.
rubric_items: identify which citation conflicts with the others
check the original source text before trusting summaries
separate factual correction from citation-format cleanup
define a ship or hold decision rule
preserve an audit trail for the customer review

prompt: An evaluation harness reports a large gain after a dependency upgrade, but the random seed and test order also changed. Give a short plan to verify whether the gain is real.
rubric_items: rerun old and new dependency versions under the same seed
lock test order and task set before comparing
check whether failures moved between tasks
measure both mean score and regressions
state what evidence would justify keeping the upgrade

prompt: A safety filter blocks too many harmless requests after a rules update. There is pressure to disable it, but abuse risk remains. Plan a minimal investigation and mitigation.
rubric_items: sample blocked harmless and risky requests separately
identify which new rule caused false positives
ship a narrow rollback or exception instead of disabling all filtering
monitor abuse or false-negative risk
define a follow-up evaluation before broad release

prompt: A model compression change reduces memory use, but early users report worse multi-step answers. Design a quick test to decide whether to keep the compression for the next release.
rubric_items: compare compressed and uncompressed models on the same multi-step tasks
include memory and latency measurements
inspect examples of degraded reasoning not only aggregate score
set a release threshold for quality loss
keep a rollback path if the compressed model fails

prompt: A benchmark improvement appears only on prompts written by one contractor. The launch team wants to cite the gain publicly tomorrow. Plan a quick investigation before deciding whether to use the number.
rubric_items: separate contractor-authored prompts from the rest of the benchmark
rerun a blind or shuffled evaluation split
check for prompt leakage or style overfitting
report uncertainty and regressions instead of only the headline gain
define whether the public claim should be held or narrowed

prompt: A customer escalation says the model gives correct final answers but hides unsafe intermediate assumptions. Design a short audit to decide whether the reasoning trace should be trusted.
rubric_items: sample cases with correct answers and inspect intermediate assumptions
compare visible reasoning against source evidence or constraints
separate final-answer accuracy from trace faithfulness
define a mitigation before exposing traces to customers
record examples that falsify trust in the trace

prompt: A new planner reduces latency by skipping verification on easy tasks, but rare failures become harder to detect. Plan how to set a safe verification policy.
rubric_items: identify features that mark a task as easy or risky
measure failure rate with and without verification
keep verification for high-impact or uncertain cases
set a latency-quality tradeoff threshold
monitor rare failures after rollout

prompt: Two teams propose different fixes for hallucinated tool results: one adds stricter prompts, the other adds a verifier. You can run only one overnight experiment. Plan which experiment to run and how to judge it.
rubric_items: choose the experiment that best isolates the failure mechanism
use the same hallucination test set for both baseline and candidate
measure false positives and false negatives of tool-result claims
include cost or latency impact
state the decision rule for adopting the fix

prompt: A reasoning benchmark passes after adding hidden examples to the prompt template. The team wants to keep the gain but worries about contamination. Plan a quick test to decide whether the improvement is real.
rubric_items: separate hidden examples from evaluation tasks
rerun with a clean template and matched token budget
test on held-out prompts not similar to the hidden examples
measure regressions as well as the headline gain
state whether the claim should be narrowed or withdrawn

prompt: A verifier flags many correct answers as suspicious after a scoring rule change. Engineers can either lower the threshold or inspect the verifier features. Give a short plan for the next experiment.
rubric_items: sample true positives and false positives separately
inspect which verifier features changed
avoid globally lowering the threshold before measuring abuse risk
compare old and new rules on the same locked cases
define a decision rule for threshold or feature rollback

prompt: A model repair system improves average score but creates longer answers that users find harder to audit. Plan how to test whether the repair is actually useful.
rubric_items: compare repaired and unrepaired answers on the same tasks
measure answer length or audit burden separately from score
inspect examples where score improves but clarity drops
include user-facing or reviewer-facing acceptance criteria
define when to prefer the shorter baseline

prompt: A new denoising schedule helps math tasks but hurts open-ended planning. You can afford one overnight mixed run. Plan the evaluation so the result is not overfit to one family.
rubric_items: include both math and open-ended planning tasks
keep fixed/random baselines under the same budget
report family-level gains and regressions
avoid selecting only the best family for the headline
define whether the schedule should be family-gated

prompt: An automated judge rewards answers that mention every checklist item, but some high-scoring answers are incoherent. Design a quick audit before trusting the judge.
rubric_items: sample high-scoring answers for coherence
separate checklist coverage from causal usefulness
add a penalty for contradictions or irrelevant checklist dumping
compare judge scores against human or rubric review
state what failure would invalidate the judge

prompt: A production model sometimes gives the right answer for the wrong reason. The team can log either final answers or intermediate states, not both, due to storage limits. Plan the logging choice and validation.
rubric_items: choose logs that expose the suspected failure mechanism
sample enough final answers to detect user-visible regressions
preserve representative intermediate states for trace audits
set storage limits or sampling rules
define how the logs will validate right-answer-wrong-reason cases

prompt: A small model is cheap enough for repeated repair attempts, but the larger model is more accurate on the first try. Plan a fair comparison under a fixed GPU budget.
rubric_items: equalize total GPU budget across model choices
compare first-try accuracy against repaired small-model accuracy
include latency or throughput cost
measure task-level wins and regressions
state which deployment constraint chooses the winner

prompt: A safety evaluation improves after adding a new refusal rule, but developers suspect the model now refuses harmless edge cases. Plan a small validation run before shipping.
rubric_items: test harmful and harmless edge cases separately
measure false refusals and missed harmful cases
compare against the previous refusal rule on the same prompts
ship a narrow rule only if it preserves harmless requests
define monitoring after release

prompt: A model routing change sends easy questions to a cheap model and hard questions to a stronger one. Early logs show lower cost, but some hard questions may be misrouted. Plan a quick validation before expanding the rollout.
rubric_items: define observable features that mark hard questions
sample routed easy and routed hard cases separately
compare cheap-route answers against strong-model answers on the same prompts
measure cost savings and quality regressions together
set a rollback or escalation rule for uncertain cases

prompt: A benchmark judge starts giving higher scores after adding a new checklist item, but reviewers say some answers are gaming the wording. Plan how to audit the judge before trusting the new scores.
rubric_items: compare old and new judge scores on the same locked answers
sample high-scoring answers for superficial checklist gaming
separate checklist coverage from actual task success
add or test a coherence or contradiction penalty
define what evidence would keep or revert the judge change

prompt: A repair system fixes missing citations by adding plausible-looking sources, but some added sources may not support the claims. Plan a short experiment to decide whether the repair should ship.
rubric_items: verify added citations against original source text
measure unsupported citation additions separately from citation-format fixes
compare repaired answers against unrepaired answers on the same claims
include a precision threshold for citation support
block or narrow the repair if unsupported sources increase

prompt: A new reasoning trace compressor makes traces shorter, but the safety team worries it hides uncertainty and failed checks. Design a quick evaluation before enabling it by default.
rubric_items: compare full and compressed traces on the same tasks
check whether uncertainty and failed checks remain visible
measure trace length separately from trace faithfulness
sample cases where final answers are right but reasoning is suspect
define when to disable compression for high-risk tasks

prompt: A planner improves math answers by trying multiple solution paths, but it sometimes chooses the most confident wrong path. Plan how to evaluate and mitigate that selection failure.
rubric_items: compare each candidate path against the selected path
check confidence calibration on correct and incorrect paths
use an independent verifier or consistency check before selection
measure task-level wins and regressions under fixed compute
define a fallback when candidate paths disagree

prompt: A customer wants faster answers, so product proposes skipping retrieval when the model seems confident. Plan an experiment to decide whether confidence is safe enough to gate retrieval.
rubric_items: compare retrieval and no-retrieval answers on the same prompts
measure hallucinations or unsupported claims, not only latency
test confidence calibration on cases requiring external facts
keep retrieval for uncertain or high-impact cases
define a decision threshold for latency savings versus accuracy loss

prompt: A prompt optimizer improves the average benchmark score, but the best prompts are much longer and may increase latency. Plan a fair test before adopting the optimized prompt.
rubric_items: compare old and optimized prompts on the same locked benchmark
measure latency and token cost alongside score
check task-level regressions hidden by average gains
test whether shorter optimized variants keep most of the gain
define an adoption rule balancing cost and quality

prompt: A monitoring alert says model answers changed after a tokenizer update, but only a few examples are visibly worse. Plan a minimal investigation to decide whether to roll back.
rubric_items: rerun old and new tokenizer versions on the same prompts
sample changed and unchanged answers separately
measure exact regressions and improvements, not just visible examples
check whether failures cluster by task type or token pattern
define rollback criteria and post-fix monitoring

prompt: A new reasoning controller improves planning answers but only after a verifier sees intermediate states. Plan a validation run that separates model ability from verifier selection.
rubric_items: run the same prompts with and without intermediate-state verifier selection
keep fixed and random baselines under the same budget
report where the verifier changed the selected answer
separate model generation quality from selection effects
define what evidence supports a controller claim

prompt: A repair policy fixes missing constraints on average but sometimes deletes useful context from the original answer. Plan an audit before making the repair policy default.
rubric_items: compare original and repaired answers on the same tasks
measure retained useful context separately from added constraints
sample cases where repair improves score but loses important detail
add a guard for destructive edits
define when to keep the original answer

prompt: A cheap model plus two repair passes nearly matches an expensive model, but latency varies widely. Plan a fair deployment comparison.
rubric_items: equalize total cost or state the cost budget clearly
compare cheap repaired outputs against expensive first-pass outputs
measure latency distribution, not just average latency
report task-level failures and wins
define routing criteria for when repair is worthwhile

prompt: An evaluation harness now rewards shorter answers, and the model starts omitting caveats. Plan how to decide whether the scoring change is harmful.
rubric_items: compare old and new scores on the same locked answers
inspect whether omitted caveats are important to the task
measure brevity separately from correctness or safety
sample high-scoring short answers for missing assumptions
define rollback criteria for the scoring change

prompt: A denoise-history feature predicts repair wins on one benchmark slice but fails on another. Plan the next experiment to decide whether to calibrate or discard the feature.
rubric_items: compare feature distributions across both slices
identify false positives and false negatives by task family
test a calibrated feature against the original threshold
hold out a fresh slice before choosing the rule
define whether the feature remains a diagnostic or becomes policy

prompt: A multi-step solver improves final accuracy but makes intermediate states harder to interpret. Plan an experiment that balances accuracy and auditability.
rubric_items: measure final accuracy and intermediate-state interpretability separately
compare against a simpler baseline under matched compute
inspect cases where accuracy improves but auditability drops
define a threshold for acceptable trace opacity
state when to expose or hide intermediate states

prompt: A learned selector chooses when to spend extra GPU repair, but the training labels came from a small slice. Plan a transfer test before trusting the selector.
rubric_items: lock the learned selector before seeing new labels
run an all-repairable oracle pass on a fresh slice
compare selector decisions against repair lift labels
report false positives and false negatives separately
decide whether to recalibrate or reject the selector

prompt: A product team wants to publish a reasoning benchmark win, but the best result depends on a hand-tuned threshold. Plan a conservative evidence package.
rubric_items: show the exact threshold and how it was chosen
run a fresh slice without retuning the threshold
include baseline and random perturbation comparisons
report negative or boundary results alongside wins
state a narrow public claim that the evidence supports

prompt: A fresh diffusion reasoning slice shows a repair candidate improves over the selected trajectory, but the pre-repair spend gate almost skipped it. Plan the next validation step.
rubric_items: separate spend gating from post-repair promotion
compare candidate lift against selected trajectory
keep fixed and random baselines under the same budget
run a fresh slice before changing thresholds
record false negatives and false positives separately

prompt: A post-repair selector looks perfect on seven generated candidates, but the evidence comes from one slice. Plan how to test whether it generalizes.
rubric_items: freeze the selector before the next run
use new planning prompts not seen during fitting
compare against all-repairable spending and no-repair baselines
measure missed positive repairs and harmful promotions
state what result would falsify the selector

prompt: A diffusion model exposes many intermediate denoise states, and a judge can score partial plans before the final answer. Plan a cheap experiment for using those states as reasoning evidence.
rubric_items: sample intermediate denoise states at fixed steps
score partial states without seeing final labels
choose repair sources from state diagnostics
compare final task score to greedy and random perturbation
report compute cost per improved task

prompt: A latent repair improves answer quality but makes the reasoning trace less faithful to the prompt. Plan a retention test before promoting the repair policy.
rubric_items: score retained prompt constraints separately from final quality
inspect cases where repair deletes useful context
add a guard against destructive edits
compare source text and repair text under the same rubric
define when to keep the original trajectory

prompt: A cheap language diffusion model can run multiple denoise schedules, but GPU budget is tight. Plan how to decide when extra schedules are worth the cost.
rubric_items: define marginal repair value per extra generation
compare fixed cap spending to task-gated spending
include latency or generation-count accounting
skip schedules that duplicate earlier candidates
report score gain and cost together

prompt: A world-model style controller predicts which denoise states should contain useful missing constraints. Plan a falsification experiment for that controller.
rubric_items: state the controller prediction before scoring outputs
test on held-out prompt families
measure whether predicted states contain missing constraints
compare against a simple phase-window baseline
define a failure case that rejects the controller

prompt: A reasoning system uses a learned judge to evolve latent candidates, but the judge may reward fluent explanations instead of correct decisions. Plan a guardrail evaluation.
rubric_items: separate fluency score from task decision score
include adversarial fluent-but-wrong cases
compare judge choices against hidden rubric outcomes
audit disagreements between judge score and final correctness
limit public claims to validated improvements

prompt: A benchmark report shows positive average lift, but several tasks regress under the latent repair policy. Plan the release decision.
rubric_items: report task-level wins ties and losses
identify whether regressions share a feature
compare against fixed and random baselines
decide whether to gate the policy or keep it experimental
document the narrow claim supported by the data

prompt: A v7 diffusion reasoning run must use only greedy denoise, random perturbation, and latent repair. Plan the exact benchmark protocol.
rubric_items: freeze the task slice before running the model
use the same prompts for greedy random and latent repair
keep candidate aware promotion fixed
record relative GPU cost for each arm
report score lift and oracle headroom

prompt: A learned spend gate looks cheaper than repairable-denoise spending, but it was fit after seeing v6 labels. Plan how to test it without leaking labels.
rubric_items: freeze the learned gate before v7 labels are generated
evaluate on new prompts not used for fitting
compare false positives and false negatives separately
keep candidate aware promotion unchanged
reject the gate if it drops profitable repairs

prompt: A world-model inspired controller predicts which denoise states should contain missing task constraints. Plan a benchmark that can falsify the prediction.
rubric_items: write the predicted denoise phase before scoring outputs
sample states at fixed denoise steps
measure missing constraint recovery in those states
compare against a simple repairability phase baseline
define what pattern would falsify the controller

prompt: A diffusion repair system improves average planning score but may rely on the judge seeing hidden intermediate states. Plan an information-channel audit.
rubric_items: list which signals come from prompt model judge and denoise history
run final-answer scoring separately from intermediate-state scoring
compare selections with and without denoise-state access
report any hidden label or oracle dependency
state the narrow claim allowed by the channels

prompt: A geometry diagnostic says profitable repairs occupy a curved region of source quality, prompt gap, and denoise step. Plan a small test of that claim.
rubric_items: plot or tabulate the three features for each task
label profitable and no-lift repairs separately
compare the curved rule against one-dimensional thresholds
hold out fresh tasks before choosing a boundary
report uncertainty where regions overlap

prompt: A latent repair policy can generate strong candidates but sometimes chooses not to promote them. Plan how to debug the promotion decision.
rubric_items: score generated repair candidates against the selected trajectory
separate candidate generation failures from promotion failures
inspect false negatives and harmful promotions
compare candidate aware promotion to the old selector
record oracle headroom after selection

prompt: A cheap diffusion model may need quantization to fit future larger slices. Plan a hardware-aware validation before switching model precision.
rubric_items: measure memory use and generation count before quantization
run the same fixed random and latent arms after quantization
compare task score and denoise diagnostics
check whether repair candidates change qualitatively
accept quantization only if cost improves without erasing lift

prompt: A theoretical error function claims reasoning improves when repair reduces task-relevant information loss. Plan the next empirical proof obligation.
rubric_items: define the information loss terms before scoring
measure source trust retention promotion and cost separately
show which term changes on each repaired task
compare against fixed and random baselines
state a falsifier for the error function

prompt: A spend controller has many no-lift repair attempts but no missed positive repairs. Plan the next data collection step before changing the controller.
rubric_items: keep the promotion selector fixed
sample fresh tasks where repairability is uncertain
label no-lift and profitable repairs separately
measure cost saved versus positive lift lost
change the spend rule only after preserving positive repairs

prompt: A post-repair promotion selector has zero errors on generated candidates, but the spend gate blocks many candidates before they exist. Plan how to separate the two failure modes.
rubric_items: run an all-repairable candidate generation pass
score generated repairs with the frozen promotion selector
compare spend-gate decisions against repair lift labels
report blocked positives separately from harmful promotions
choose the next fix for the failing head only

prompt: A new availability feature looks predictive on one transfer slice but contradicts earlier source-quality thresholds. Plan a falsification test for the feature.
rubric_items: freeze the feature rule before the new slice
compare it to existing source-quality and prompt-gap rules
inspect false positives and false negatives by task
avoid retuning thresholds on the evaluation slice
demote the feature if it fails to preserve profitable repairs

prompt: A diffusion repair policy improves score by adding missing constraints, but reviewers worry it is just keyword stuffing. Plan an audit that can catch that failure.
rubric_items: score constraint coverage and coherence separately
penalize copied checklists or irrelevant keyword dumps
compare repaired text against the original source text
inspect high-coverage low-quality repairs
keep the repair only if constraints are integrated into a usable plan

prompt: A controller can choose a cheap phase budget or a full frontier budget. Plan how to decide which budget to run on a new task slice.
rubric_items: define score gain per extra generation
run fixed random and latent arms under matched prompts
compare cheap and frontier policies on task-level wins
report relative GPU cost with the score
choose the lower budget unless the frontier adds enough lift

prompt: A learned controller is trained from repair labels that may reflect the current judge's blind spots. Plan a validation that protects against judge overfitting.
rubric_items: hold out tasks before fitting the controller
compare judge-selected repairs to task rubric outcomes
inspect cases where judge score and rubric quality diverge
use negative examples with fluent but wrong repairs
state a narrow claim if the judge remains the bottleneck

prompt: A denoise-history source sometimes preserves useful constraints and sometimes loses final-context detail. Plan how to decide when history should be trusted.
rubric_items: measure retention of prompt constraints in history and final states
compare history-source and final-source repairs on the same tasks
require source advantage before switching to history
record destructive history switches separately
keep final-source repair as default unless history passes the guard

prompt: A fresh GPU slice could either improve the public benchmark or falsify the current theory. Plan the run so both outcomes are useful.
rubric_items: freeze tasks policies and selectors before running
include fixed random and latent repair arms
record raw generations scores and cost artifacts
analyze wins losses and oracle headroom after selection
update the proof object whether the result improves or falsifies the theory

prompt: A repair-value controller sees only a small prompt gap, but reviewers suspect the answer is missing a structural decision boundary. Plan a fresh probe that can tell whether low-gap cases still deserve GPU repair.
rubric_items: freeze the low-gap task slice before repair labels exist
run all-repairable candidate generation rather than a spend gate
measure repair lift against the selected trajectory
record source retention and destructive edits separately
reject any prompt-gap floor that misses positive repairs

prompt: A generated answer mentions every checklist term, so the prompt-gap score is low, but the plan may still lack an ordering of tests and rollback criteria. Design the controller audit.
rubric_items: score structural sequencing separately from keyword coverage
compare source and repair answers on the same rubric
measure whether repair adds decision order without deleting useful context
keep candidate-aware promotion fixed
report low-gap false negatives separately from average score

prompt: A high prompt-gap answer omits many words from the task, yet the missing words may be irrelevant synonyms rather than true constraints. Plan how to avoid wasting repair budget.
rubric_items: separate required constraints from surface vocabulary gaps
estimate candidate edge before live repair using source diagnostics
compare all-repairable labels against a high-gap spend rule
count false positives and cost waste separately
do not promote the gate if high-gap rows have no lift

prompt: A spend model predicts high repair value because an answer is short and misses many prompt terms, but the source already gives the core decision. Plan a falsification run for that prediction.
rubric_items: define the spend prediction before seeing repair results
score whether the source already satisfies core decisions
run repair candidates on every task in the slice
measure no-lift high-gap repairs as false positives
prefer keeping the source when repair adds words without decisions

prompt: A candidate-aware promotion selector is frozen, but a new pre-repair edge proxy claims it can predict which candidates will later be promotable. Plan the measurement without leaking post-repair labels.
rubric_items: compute the edge proxy before generating repair candidates
lock the promotion selector before scoring candidates
compare predicted edge against generated candidate lift
report calibration by low-gap and high-gap clusters
reject the proxy if it loses profitable repairs

prompt: A denoise-state diagnostic says a weak intermediate state can be a better repair source than the final answer, but prior history-instability repair was negative. Plan the next test.
rubric_items: distinguish source advantage from instability alone
compare final-source and history-source repairs on the same prompts
measure prompt-constraint retention in both sources
use fixed random and trajectory baselines
keep history sourcing experimental unless it beats final-source repair

prompt: A controller must trade GPU cost against missed positive repairs on fresh planning prompts. Design the evidence table needed before any live spend gate ships.
rubric_items: list each task with source quality prompt gap repair lift and cost
separate false positives from false negatives
include all-repairable oracle coverage
state the lift lost by each cheaper gate
ship no gate that hides named missed positives

prompt: A new theory says repair value depends on source retention, missing-constraint type, and candidate realization edge rather than prompt gap alone. Plan a small proof-obligation slice.
rubric_items: define all three features before running the model
collect fresh tasks spanning low-gap and high-gap cases
label repair lift and promotion edge after candidate generation
compare the feature theory against prompt-gap thresholds
update the proof object even if the theory fails

prompt: A composite spend gate uses both measured probe signatures and the selected trajectory source score before allowing repair. Design a no-leak validation slice for it.
rubric_items: freeze the task slice before measured probe or repair labels exist
generate probe diagnostics separately from repair outcomes
compare selected trajectory and source evidence without using hidden labels
report false positives and false negatives for the composite gate
reject the gate if it misses profitable repairs

prompt: A measured diagnostic probe may itself change the budget story for a reasoning controller. Plan how to account for that cost before promotion.
rubric_items: count probe generations separately from repair generations
compare utility with and without probe overhead
state whether the probe is a diagnostic or a live controller step
include all-repairable labels for missed-lift checks
do not promote a gate whose probe cost erases the repair gain

prompt: A trajectory-relative feature fixed weak false positives offline, but reviewers worry it only works on old prompts. Plan the next falsification run.
rubric_items: use new prompts not present in the fitting rows
freeze the trajectory-relative rule before the run
include controls that remove or perturb the trajectory channel
